creator: Alexander Terp
description:
amterp, Chat Notes 2026-10-14: "potentially remove uniqueness requirement on pane renames, leverage the muster generated names more instead".

Today the daemon refuses a rename to a name another open pane on that machine holds (`name_held` in `rename_pane`, `crates/muster-daemon/src/session.rs`), because `--pane` and `msg post --to` resolve a name to exactly one pane. The proposal: a given name becomes a label that may repeat, so two panes can both be `reviewer`, and the drawn word (`otter`), already unique per machine, is what commands resolve.

What it would take:

- The word has to stay reserved through a rename. Today a renamed pane keeps its word on its record, but another pane can be given that word as its name.
- `--pane reviewer` matching two panes needs an answer. Refusing and naming both, as a clash does today, is the obvious one.
- Messaging names agents by their pane names: group membership, `whom`, and how participants are printed (a_2dog2o3cN, a_2dnEiGhpm).
- `name_sessions` names a Claude Code session after the given name, so two sessions would share a name.

Related: a_2j16WrhNT, showing the drawn word on every agent row.
title: Should a pane's given name stop having to be unique, with its drawn word as the handle?
